Subject: Long-context evaluation for CareCo — sample data and next steps

Sergio,

Thanks for taking the call this morning. Quick recap from our side: CareCo needs an evaluation focused on very long clinical records (~40k-70k token sequences per patient). Main priorities are: entity/relation preservation across long spans, truncation behavior (what gets dropped), and summarization fidelity for downstream clinical review. Latency is secondary for the pilot.

I've attached a redacted sample of patient transcripts (careco_transcripts_sample.csv) and our scoring rubric (careco_rubric_v1.pdf). Can you confirm the following so we can align internally:
- Which Redwood model variants you recommend for initial benchmarks (encoder-decoder vs decoder-only, and quantization profiles)
- Whether you can run evals directly in a customer VPC or we need to provide data snapshots to Redwood's sandbox
- An estimated timeline and high-level plan (prompt sets, eval metrics, reporting format)

If helpful, Stanley (product lead) is looping in procurement/infosec later this week.

Best,
Anya Kovacs
Head of Clinical AI
MedTech AI

Hi Anya — thanks for the materials and the clear rubric. Short recap and proposed plan below.

Recap from our discovery:
- Goal: Validate factual fidelity and truncation behavior on 40k-70k token clinical records.
- Success criteria: >= 85% on your entity recall rubric and no systemic hallucination in episode summaries.

Recommended models for pilot (starting points):
- redwood-7b-long-v1 (decoder-only, optimized KV cache handling) — good balance of cost and long-range coherence
- redwood-13b-llm-long-q4 (13B quantized) — better factuality on summarization tests, higher RAM needs
- For a high-precision arm: redwood-34b-long (non-quantized) — run as a gold standard for regression checks

Evaluation plan (proposed):
1) Ingest: We can accept your redacted CSV into a customer sandbox (VPC) for pilot runs — preferred for compliance.
2) Prompt set: We'll use the rubric to construct ~120 prompts covering extraction, summarization, and chain-of-thought checks. Draft prompt set attached (redwood_promptset_v1.json).
3) Runs: Batch runs across the three model variants, with KV/caching enabled and sequence window set to 70k tokens where supported.
4) Metrics: entity recall/precision, summarization ROUGE + clinical-fidelity human spot checks, truncation delta (what tokens were dropped and where summaries lost context).
5) Reporting: A short executive summary, a per-model benchmark, and diffs vs your rubric.

Timeline (estimate):
- Week 0 (this week): NDA/procurement + sandbox access
- Week 1: Prompt finalization + smoke runs (small subset)
- Week 2: Full runs + human spot-checks
- Week 3: Deliver report + recommendations

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm VPC sandbox access or share a secure upload path
- We kick off an NDA and scope estimate (I attached pilot_scope_estimate.xlsx)
- Vivek will own the eval execution; Laura will own commercial/discount conversations.

Linking our HubSpot pilot page: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/CARECO-PL-2026-03

Happy to jump on a short call to align on the rubrics if helpful.

Cheers,
Sergio Alvarez

On Mon, Mar 15, 2026 at 4:30 PM Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com> wrote:
> Recap from our discovery:
> - Goal: Validate factual fidelity and truncation behavior on 40k-70k token clinical records.

Hi all — quick technical notes from the infra/eval side. I'm happy to run the benchmark once we have the data in a sandbox. A few caveats & implementation choices to call out: 

1) Effective context vs window size:
- Even if we set the model window to 70k tokens, effective context is influenced by KV cache behavior and batching; we should measure per-request token retention.

2) Tokenization mismatch and entity drift:
- Clinical text often includes shorthand and nonstandard punctuation; recommend canonicalization preprocessing (we can supply a small normalization step).

3) Truncation logging:
- We'll produce a truncation report that maps original offsets to what the model actually saw. That helps you understand where summaries lose antecedent info.

4) Quantization impacts:
- Q4 int8/quants reduce memory but can slightly degrade numeric fidelity and rare-entity recall. For the gold-standard run, use non-quantized 34B.

5) Human evaluation cadence:
- For clinical fidelity we should sample ~50 records for clinician review (we'll anonymize further).

Operational ask:
- Please provision a VPC sandbox with S3-compatible object access and a service account for redwood-eval@careco (limited scope). If that's not possible, we can run inside our test VPC with encrypted uploads.

I'll stand up the runner once access is granted.

— Vivek
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
